package_info.why_malicious: These packages abuse the npm registry by storing large, non-software media files (pirated movies, videos, eBooks) split into parts, violating platform terms of service and threatening registry integrity and availability. They do not contain functional software code and are used for illicit file hosting, not legitimate development.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package delivers large video files (.ts) as part of its contents, resulting in the distribution of pirated or unauthorized media via the npm registry.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Software packages are expected to contain code or legitimate assets, not large video files. The presence of multiple large .ts files (video segments) is highly anomalous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages contain JavaScript/TypeScript code and small assets, not multi-gigabyte video content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include small demo videos or assets for a media player library, but not full-length movies split into parts.
key_indicators: Multiple large .ts files in package root
No actual code or software functionality
Package size (54.5 MB+) far exceeds typical npm package
File extensions and content unrelated to software development

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package delivers JSON files containing time-synced user comments (danmu) associated with the pirated video content, further indicating the package's use as a media distribution mechanism.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: JSON files containing time-synced comments for video playback are not expected in npm packages unless the package is a legitimate video player or similar tool. Here, they are used to support illicit media distribution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not include large, structured comment data for pirated media.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use could be in open-source video player projects with demo data, but not in bulk-uploaded, non-functional packages.
key_indicators: Presence of playlist.m3u8 files (streaming playlist format)
No code to process or use these files

attack_chain.action: Attacker splits pirated video content into multiple .ts files and prepares associated metadata (danmu.json, playlist.m3u8).
attack_chain.leads_to: Creation of large, non-software npm packages.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes hundreds of packages with wlwz- prefix, each containing a segment of the pirated media.
attack_chain.leads_to: npm registry is flooded with non-software, media-hosting packages.

attack_chain.action: Users (or automated systems) downloading these packages receive large video files and associated metadata instead of software.
attack_chain.leads_to: Registry integrity and availability are threatened; potential for further abuse (piracy, evasion of censorship, etc.).

behavioral_signatures: npm packages with no code and only large media files
Presence of multiple .ts files (video segments) in package root
Inclusion of danmu.json and playlist.m3u8 files without supporting code
Package size far exceeding typical npm package (e.g., >50MB)
file_indicators: package.json with no main entry or code
network_indicators: No network activity from the package itself, but bulk downloads of large, non-code npm packages may indicate abuse
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Flag npm packages with the following characteristics: (1) package size >50MB, (2) presence of multiple .ts files, (3) inclusion of danmu.json or playlist.m3u8 files, (4) lack of any JavaScript/TypeScript code, and (5) package names matching the wlwz-* pattern. Automated systems should alert or block such packages to prevent registry abuse and maintain supply chain hygiene.
